---
title: "Get started with updoc"
description: "Preview your pkgdown site as you edit, then build it to publish."
output: rmarkdown::html_document
---

Writing package docs usually means saving a file, running `pkgdown::build_site()`,
waiting, and refreshing your browser. updoc handles that loop for you: edit your
package, hit save, and your preview updates on its own.

## Install and start

Install updoc from GitHub:

```r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("leightonpayne/updoc")
```

updoc uses the Pandoc installation found by rmarkdown (2.10.1 or newer). If you
need to use a different copy, see the [Pandoc options](configuration.html#pandoc).

From inside your package directory, start the preview server:

```r
updoc::serve()
```

Your browser opens to the preview. (If your package already has a built site,
updoc serves a copy right away while the first fresh build runs.) Press **Ctrl+C**
in R whenever you want to stop.

If you'd rather run the preview from a separate terminal so your R session stays
free, pass `browse = TRUE` because `Rscript` isn't interactive:

```sh
Rscript -e "updoc::serve(browse = TRUE)"
```

## Edit and save as usual

Leave the preview running and work on your package normally. Whenever you save a
file, updoc figures out what needs rebuilding:

- **Vignettes and articles:** rebuilds just the file you edited.
- **Roxygen comments in `R/`:** regenerates help pages in the background and
  rebuilds the affected reference pages.
- **`README.Rmd`, `README.md`, or `NEWS.md`:** renders `README.Rmd` if needed
  and updates the home or news page.
- **Site CSS, assets, or logo:** refreshes site assets without rebuilding every
  page.
- **R code, `DESCRIPTION`, `_pkgdown.yml`, or deleted files:** runs a full site
  rebuild so nothing gets out of sync.

Everything happens in a temporary copy of your package, so previewing never
modifies your `man/` files, `NAMESPACE`, `README.md`, or `docs/` folder.

## Watching builds in the browser

The small popup at the bottom of the page tracks what updoc is doing, with Doc
(the hexagonal mascot) changing state as builds run:

- While a build is running, the popup shows live progress.
- If a build hits warnings or fails, the popup opens with the error and source
  context so you can spot the problem quickly. Your last working preview stays
  available while you fix it and save again.
- You can minimize warnings or errors to get them out of the way, and click the
  **Watching for changes** pill anytime to open the manual **Rebuild** button.

Try each state on the demo popup at the bottom of this page:

## Keep your R console free

`serve()` holds onto the R console until you press Ctrl+C. If you want to keep
running R commands while your preview updates in the background, use `preview()`
instead:

```r
site <- updoc::preview()

site                      # Print a quick status summary
site$status()             # Inspect build status, warnings, errors, and log path
site$wait()               # Wait until the current build finishes
site$rebuild()            # Trigger a rebuild manually
site$rebuild(full = TRUE) # Force a full site rebuild
site$open()               # Open the preview in your browser again
site$stop()               # Stop watching and shut down the server
```

Both `serve()` and `preview()` accept the same
[configuration options](configuration.html).

## Check without modifying files

If you want a quick one-shot verification in CI, a script, or an AI agent loop
without leaving a server running or changing files in your package, run:

```r
updoc::check()
```

Like a preview, `check()` validates your sources and builds the site in a
temporary copy, then prints a summary and exits non-zero if anything failed.
Pass `format = "json"` for machine-readable output (see
[Automation and AI agents](configuration.html#automation-and-ai-agents)).

## Build your site to publish

Because previews work in a temporary copy, they don't update the files you check
in or deploy. When you're ready to build the real site, run:

```r
updoc::build()
```

This updates your package's generated roxygen docs, renders `README.Rmd` to
`README.md` if you have one, and writes the finished site to your pkgdown output
folder (usually `docs/`). It doesn't upload anything for you, so publish that
folder using your normal hosting setup.

See the [`build()` reference](../reference/build.html) if you want to write to a
custom output folder, run a `lazy = TRUE` build, or skip regenerating roxygen
documentation.
